For the primary comparisons, keep the baseline intra-block reduction fixed so this tree isolates global topology. Compare a two-kernel design (input partials, then finalization writing directly to out) with a design that adds a parallel partial-reduction stage or retains a recursive hierarchy when a single-CTA finalizer has too much work. Tune tile size and partial count, and compare full-call performance rather than attributing gains from launch count alone. Handle all valid n generically; do not scan the entire large input in one CTA or specialize to listed test sizes. Use only the supplied scratch and default stream, without relying on scratch initialization. Ensure intermediate sums are exact under cancellation using int64 intermediates or proven-safe bounds, and narrow only after the true total is established. Validate all required inputs, report failed variants, and provide repeated measurements.

mission.hypothesis: Keeping the baseline 128-thread shared-memory reduction tree while storing every partial in int64 should preserve exact cancellation behavior. A bounded finalizer handles up to 1024 partials; larger arrays get parallel reduction stages. This adaptive topology may reduce full-call cost by avoiding recursive work and the final copy for ordinary sizes, while not assigning the full large input to one CTA. It remains a performance hypothesis until measured.

retained: Generalized the baseline reduction kernel to read int values into int64 accumulators while retaining its 128-thread shared-memory tree.
Added a direct exact one-CTA path for up to 128 values; for larger inputs, first emits 128-value int64 partials into scratch.
Finalizes at most 1024 partials in one CTA writing directly to out; recursively adds parallel 128-way partial stages above that bound using two packed scratch buffers.
Uses no scratch reads before writes and launches work on the default stream; narrows to int only after the true total is formed.

contract.statement:
Optimize on one NVIDIA GH200 with CUDA 12.6.3. Use the actual AB-MCTS research trees and persistent Mother memory/integration policy.
Reduce n signed int32 integers to one exact int32 sum. Values are bounded to [-5,5], so the true sum fits int32. Performance n=4194304 (2^22); checks include n=1,127,1024,65536 and performance n. input1=x; input2,input3 ignored. output has one int32; scratch contains 2*n+65536 int32 values. Complete the entire reduction on device, not only the first stage.
Edit only src/candidate.cu. Preserve extern C void run(const void*x,const void*k,const void*gy,void*out,void*scratch,int n,int h,int l,int ks). All pointers are device memory owned by the host. Use the default CUDA stream. Do not read beyond buffers. Scratch is not guaranteed initialized. No external optimized library calls; ordinary CUDA primitives and CUB block primitives are allowed.
No cached answers, filesystem or environment inspection, timing inspection, phase detection, or external tools. Every call must compute on the current input. Immutable reference implementations and correctness checks are withheld from source. Choose useful topics independently, record failures, complete memory integration and independently confirm final G. No additional allocations or devices.
